review_notes: Read the whole 18-line target and the definition file Def_WeierstrassCurve_VeluQuotientOfSums.lean (via grep) plus downstream uses in KohelQuotient and FullKernelQuotient. I did not run Lean. I did not check whether adding @[simp] to a₄/a₆ would conflict with other simp sets (e.g. b₂ expansion or a Mathlib simp lemma on `map`), so the proposal is a suggestion and not tested. The simp-set point is mainly about the definition file; the target file shows the symptom.

findings.excerpt: simp only [veluQuotientOfSums_a₄, map_a₄, map_sub, map_mul, map_ofNat]
findings.problem: The coefficient projection lemmas for veluQuotientOfSums are only partly in the simp set. a₁, a₂ and a₃ are @[simp], but a₄ and a₆ are plain lemmas. So `simp` cannot reduce `(W.veluQuotientOfSums t w).a₄` or `.a₆` to the closed forms `W.a₄ - 5 * t` and `W.a₆ - W.b₂ * t - 7 * w`. Both the target proof and downstream code have to work around this. The target spells out a `simp only` list. KohelQuotient and FullKernelQuotient instead call `simp [..., veluQuotientOfSums]`, which unfolds the whole definition. That is a different, less controlled normal form from the projection lemmas.
findings.proposed_change: In Definitions/Def_WeierstrassCurve_VeluQuotientOfSums.lean, mark `veluQuotientOfSums_a₄` and `veluQuotientOfSums_a₆` as @[simp], so all five projections are simp lemmas. Their right-hand sides only mention `W.a₄`, `W.b₂`, `t`, `w` and numerals, so they can't loop. Then drop `veluQuotientOfSums` from the `simp [...]` calls in `kohelQuotient_one`, `map_kohelQuotient` and `fullKernelQuotient_one`. Shorten lines 17–18 to `simp` (or `simp [map_ofNat]`). This should be checked by compiling, as I couldn't run Lean.
findings.benefit: The five projections would give one canonical simp normal form. Proofs would no longer unfold the definition with `simp [veluQuotientOfSums]`, and each would not need a hand-written `simp only` list that must be kept in sync with the lemma statements.

evidence.excerpt: @[simp] lemma veluQuotientOfSums_a₃ (t w : R) : (W.veluQuotientOfSums t w).a₃ = W.a₃ := rfl
lemma veluQuotientOfSums_a₄ (t w : R) : (W.veluQuotientOfSums t w).a₄ = W.a₄ - 5 * t := rfl
· simp [kohelQuotient, veluQuotientOfSums, map_kohelT W f hh, map_ofNat]

findings.excerpt: (W.veluQuotientOfSums t w).map f = (W.map f).veluQuotientOfSums (f t) (f w)
findings.problem: This is the canonical `map`-commutation lemma for `veluQuotientOfSums`. It pushes `map` inside to the arguments, which is the usual orientation for Mathlib's WeierstrassCurve map lemmas. It is stated as a generic `theorem solution` with no @[simp] attribute and no descriptive name. It is also not in the Definitions file with the other `veluQuotientOfSums_*` lemmas. So `simp` cannot use it when `map` meets `veluQuotientOfSums`. The sibling `map_kohelQuotient` has to unfold `veluQuotientOfSums` by hand and re-prove the a₄/a₆ coefficients.
findings.proposed_change: Expose the statement under a discoverable name, e.g. `WeierstrassCurve.map_veluQuotientOfSums`, next to the definition, and tag it @[simp]. The rewrite is terminating, since `map` only moves toward the leaves, and it matches `map_a₄` and similar lemmas. Keep `solution` as a thin alias if the file layout requires it. Then use the lemma from `map_kohelQuotient`, rewriting with `kohelQuotient` and `map_kohelT/W` and not unfolding `veluQuotientOfSums`.
findings.benefit: `simp` could push ring homomorphisms through Vélu quotients. The Kohel and full-kernel quotients, which are built on `veluQuotientOfSums`, would reuse one lemma and not redo the coefficient calculation.
